t: In the 17th century a poor kingdom of some 2.5 million people made itself the dominant power of the Baltic.
Gustavus Adolphus's military reforms reshaped European warfare and his intervention changed the course of the Thirty Years War.
Charles XII's defeat by Russia at Poltava in 1709 broke Swedish power, and the Peace of Nystad in 1721 ended the empire.
dyk: Stockholms Banco issued Europe's first banknotes in 1661, and its successor, the Sveriges Riksbank of 1668, is the oldest central bank still operating.
ev: The Peace of Stolbovo gives Sweden Ingria and Kexholm from Russia
Gustavus Adolphus intervenes in the Thirty Years War
Swedish and Saxon forces rout Tilly's Catholic League army at Breitenfeld
The Peace of Westphalia grants Sweden Western Pomerania, Bremen, Verden and Wismar
Charles X Gustav marches across the frozen Belts and forces the Treaty of Roskilde on Denmark
Peter the Great crushes Charles XII's army at Poltava
Charles XII is killed at the siege of Fredriksten in Norway
The Peace of Nystad cedes Estonia, Livonia and Ingria to Russia
